subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lead-in and dialogue: coping with university life
outcomes: Predict questions a student might ask about university life
Read a dialogue and find Faisal's problems and how Abdullah helps
Review the past simple, present perfect and past continuous

tf.s: Faisal leaves his essays to the last minute.
tf.why: Yes, this is part of his time management problem.

tf.s: Faisal is always early for class.
tf.why: Faisal is often late for class.

tf.s: Faisal finds cooking and washing his clothes challenging.
tf.why: Looking after himself is new for him.
Yes, that is one way Abdullah helps.

tf.s: Abdullah tells Faisal that finding university strange is unusual.
tf.why: He tells Faisal it is normal to find university strange.

tf.s: Faisal is finding it difficult to live alone.
tf.why: Living alone is one of his problems.

tf.s: 'I felt nervous on my first day' is in the past simple.
'I was walking to class' is in the present perfect.
At university, students only need to learn how to study.
tf.why: They also learn to manage time and live independently.

tf.s: 'I have lived here for a year' is in the present perfect.
tf.why: Have + past participle is the present perfect.

boxes.q: What is one of Faisal's problems?
boxes.why: He leaves essays late and is late for class.

boxes.q: What does Abdullah say about finding university strange?
Which tense is 'He was cooking dinner'?
Which tense is 'I have finished my essay'?
boxes.why: Have + past participle is the present perfect.

boxes.q: Which tense is 'She lost her ID card yesterday'?

boxes.why: Coping means managing a hard situation.

boxes.q: A person who can look after himself is...
boxes.why: Independent people manage on their own.

boxes.q: Who can give new students useful advice from experience?
boxes.why: Older students have already been through it.

boxes.q: What does Faisal find challenging apart from studying?
boxes.why: Looking after himself is new for him.

boxes.q: How does Abdullah help Faisal get to places?
boxes.why: Giving someone a lift means driving them.

mcq.q: What problem does Faisal have with time?
o: He leaves essays to the last minute and is late for class
He finishes everything a week early
He has no essays to write
He has too much free time
mcq.why: Poor time management causes these problems.

mcq.q: Which three past tenses are reviewed in the lead-in?
o: Past simple, present perfect and past continuous
Present simple, future and present continuous
Future perfect, present simple and future
mcq.why: These are the main tenses for talking about the past.

o: He gives him a lift and invites him to dinner
He writes his essays for him
He cooks for him every day
mcq.why: Abdullah offers practical help and support.

o: Able to look after yourself without help

mcq.q: Choose the sentence in the past simple.
o: I felt nervous on my first day.

mcq.why: The past continuous shows an action in progress when another happened.

mcq.q: Complete: 'I ___ three essays this term so far.'
mcq.why: 'So far' goes with the present perfect.

mcq.q: Why is it useful to learn from older students?
o: They can give advice from their own experience
mcq.why: They have already faced the same problems.

mcq.q: Faisal leaves essays to the last minute. What skill does he need most?
mcq.why: Planning his time would solve this problem.

mcq.q: Why does Abdullah tell Faisal it is normal to find university strange?
o: To reassure him and make him feel better
mcq.why: Knowing others feel the same is comforting.
